commits.message:
fix(table,columns,layout): clear end on a RichText embedded directly, not just via string

/code-review high on rich-text-5ai found that table.ts's toRenderable
passthrough arm returns a directly-embedded RichText untouched (it
implements render, so it never reaches toCellText's end-clearing), and
that layout.ts's constructor/update only clear end on the string
branch. Both draw a stray extra blank line once RichText.render honors
end for non-empty text. columns.ts had the identical passthrough gap,
caught by the same grep pattern while fixing table.ts.

All three now route a directly-passed RichText through the same
copy-and-clear treatment the string branch already gets, matching the
convention panel.ts and tree.ts already follow. Regression tests added
for each.

fix(text): end draws the same trailing segment for empty and non-empty text (rich-text-5ai)

RichText.render() gave `end` two meanings: honored for empty text (any
truthy value, including the default "\n"), but silently dropped for
non-empty text unless it was a non-default value. `end: ""` was a
no-op on the common (non-empty) path even though every internal
embedding site (columns, table cells, tree labels, panel content, now
progress's TextColumn) already set it defensively.

One rule now: `end` is its own trailing segment whenever it is a
non-empty string, for empty and non-empty text alike. Console.print
already clears a text item's `end` before rendering it (rich-console-dcg),
so printed output is unaffected. Callers that render a RichText directly
and embed it as a line rather than a printed unit now need to clear
`end` themselves, matching the existing convention — Panel's bare-string
content and TextColumn's markup output were the two gaps, fixed here.

fix(console): end belongs to text; a renderable ends its own lines (rich-console-dcg) (#144)

* fix(console): end belongs to text; a renderable ends its own lines (rich-console-dcg)

Two consecutive prints of a Panel, Table or Rule left a blank line between
them: the renderable closed its last line and print then appended `end`
regardless.

The ticket framed the choice as an intended aesthetic or a column-tracking
console, and described Python Rich as the second. Rich 15.0.0 is neither. It
attaches `sep` and `end` only to runs of text items and lets any other
renderable own its line breaks. Column tracking would also have been wrong:
`print("a\n")` is "a\n\n" in Rich and must stay so, and only the item's kind,
not the cursor column, separates that trailing break from a Panel's.

Console.print now builds a PrintBlock list. A run of adjacent text items
(strings, RichText, data) is joined by `sep` and ended by `end`. Any other
renderable is a block whose lines are each closed by the print. This also
fixes the mixed cases, which matched Rich in none of these ways before:
`print("a", panel, "b")` put the panel's top edge on the "a" line and led
"b" with a space, and `end` was appended after a renderable.

One deliberate divergence from Rich remains: a renderable that leaves its last
line open, such as Strip, has it closed here, so the next print and the
export start on a new line.

Line ends added by print stay outside the print and console styles, as Rich
emits them.

Docs: docs/console.md gains a "Line ends" section. The blank line drawn in
docs/group.md and explained in docs/pretty.md is gone.

* fix(console): a RichText argument runs with the print's end, not its own

A RichText passed to print joined the text run as it was, so its own `end`
still rendered. RichText writes `end` for empty text and for any non-default
value. So `print("a", new RichText(""), "b")` broke the line mid-run as
"a \n b\n", `print(new RichText(""))` printed two line breaks, and
`print(new RichText("a", { end: "!" }), "b")` put "!" inside the line.
Python Rich ignores an item's own `end` in all three cases.

The RichText arm now runs a copy with `end` cleared, as the string arm already
does, and the caller's object is left untouched.

The block comment now also says where this port's text/block split differs
from the reference: data. Rich gives a container lines of its own. That
question is filed as rich-console-5k3.
